title: Heavy Rain Floods the Four Corners Region
summary:
Heavy rain that started on Wednesday has caused flooding in the Four Corners region, where New Mexico, Colorado, Utah, and Arizona meet. By Friday, October 23, floodwaters had closed roads, forced evacuations, and led to emergency declarations in the four states. Forecasters said more rain could come through Sunday.

In San Juan County, New Mexico, Devin Neeley described blue sky above while brown floodwaters filled low-lying homes below. He said the county had not seen flooding like this in generations, and people in vulnerable areas were told to evacuate on Thursday afternoon.

In Hurricane, southern Utah, flooding damaged more than 100 homes and recreational vehicles. Navajo Nation police said authorities rescued seven families, 30 people. The Hopi Tribe in Arizona declared a state of emergency, and Colorado Governor Jared Polis declared disaster emergencies for 11 counties.

In Farmington, New Mexico, Police Chief Steve Hebbe said no deaths had been reported, and urged people not to take the flooding lightly. Meteorologists said the rain came from the remnants of Hurricane Trudy.
why_it_matters: Floods can close roads and schools near your home, so knowing why people evacuate helps you stay safe when heavy rain comes.
